module: Identify actors and design interaction disclosure

lesson.title: AI systems, models and the EU connection
lesson.summary: Recognise the system, separate its model and establish the EU connection.

blocks: We follow **Harbour Services**, a fictional organisation building a customer assistant and a media workflow. Its people, suppliers and scenarios are invented. This course teaches Article 50 transparency; each conclusion still needs the actual facts of a real use.

An **AI system** is machine-based, operates with some autonomy and infers from inputs how to produce predictions, content, recommendations or decisions for explicit or implicit objectives. Its outputs can influence physical or digital environments; it may adapt after deployment.

sources.title: Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: Inference matters. A learned assistant deriving an answer from inputs differs from a fixed rule that sorts a list by date. Automation or an 'AI' product label alone does not settle the definition.
Human review does not itself remove AI status. Continuing retraining is optional, not a condition every deployed system must satisfy.

sources.title: Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: A **general-purpose AI model** has significant generality and can perform many distinct tasks. A model can be integrated into systems. A **general-purpose AI system** is based on such a model and can serve varied purposes directly or through integration.

Harbour adds an interface, documents and actions around an external model. Assess the operated assistant as a system. Article 50 addresses specified systems; a model provider's separate model obligations require their own analysis.

sources.title: Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: The **EU scope check** asks how supply or use connects to the Union. Article 2 includes providers placing systems or models on the EU market, deployers established or located in the EU, and certain third-country actors where system output is used in the EU.

An overseas server does not automatically exclude Harbour's EU-facing assistant. Record the relevant actor, supply and use facts; check the exact paragraph rather than deciding solely from server location.

sources.title: Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation

blocks: Article 2(10) excludes obligations of deployers who use systems in purely personal, non-professional activity. That is not a universal exemption for suppliers serving private people.

Article 2(12)'s free/open-source system exclusion is conditional: high-risk, Article 5 and Article 50 systems remain outside that exclusion. Harbour cannot dismiss transparency simply because it uses open weights. Other exclusions need their own exact tests.

sources.title: Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
